findings.failure_path: With diff.noprefix=true, let the base contain identical file.txt and nested/file.txt. The reviewed commit changes nested/file.txt; HEAD instead changes file.txt after integrating a disjoint target update. The path guard checks nested/file.txt and passes. The generated patch lacks a/ and b/ prefixes, so git apply's default -p1 strips nested/ and applies the reviewed hunk to file.txt. The resulting index equals HEAD, silently covering an unreviewed relocated edit.
findings.smallest_fix: Pin default source and destination prefixes when generating the patch, and add a regression using diff.noprefix=true with identical nested and root files.

findings.failure_path: Run the hook from a subdirectory with diff.relative=true. Put A21's repeated-block file outside that subdirectory: the target rewrites the reviewed block and HEAD edits the look-alike block. The name collection and patch generation explicitly disable relative filtering, but this disjointness check does not. It excludes the outside file and succeeds; git apply then relocates the hunk as in the previous finding, reproducing HEAD and incorrectly silencing the reminder.
findings.smallest_fix: Add --no-relative to the disjointness comparison and test A21 from a subdirectory with diff.relative=true.

findings.failure_path: A23 appends target content far from the reviewed hunk and then cleanly cherry-picks the reviewed commit. This is a conflict-free integration with unchanged reviewed changes, yet the new test requires a reminder solely because both sides touched the same file. That contradicts the frozen acceptance requiring clean target integrations and unchanged-patch rebases to retain coverage.
findings.smallest_fix: Allow nonoverlapping target edits while preventing hunk relocation, and make this clean-integration case expect quiet coverage.
